prediction.raw: 0 The idea that a child deserves ice cream solely because they got good grades can be problematic. While it's natural to want to celebrate achievements, tying rewards like ice cream to grades can create an unhealthy association between food and performance. It may also encourage extrinsic motivation (working for rewards) rather than intrinsic motivation (working for personal satisfaction or growth). Additionally, using food as a reward can contribute to an unhealthy relationship with food. A better approach might be to celebrate good grades with non-food rewards or by acknowledging the effort and hard work behind the achievement.
